CHAPTER.VERS: Wine a mocker, strong drink raging: and whoever is deceived by it is not wise.
The fear of a king as the roaring of a lion: provoketh him to anger sinneth his own soul.
an honour for a man to cease from strife: but every fool will be meddling.

The sluggard will not plow by reason of the cold; shall he beg in harvest, and nothing.
cold: or, winter
Counsel in the heart of man deep water; but a man of understanding will draw it out.

Most men will proclaim every one his own goodness: but a faithful man who can find?
goodness: or, bounty
The just walketh in his integrity: his children blessed after him.
A king that sitteth on the throne of judgment scattereth away all evil with his eyes.
Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?

Differing weights, differing measures, both of them alike abomination to the LORD.
Divers weights: Heb. A stone and a stone
divers measures: Heb. an ephah and an ephah
Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work pure, and whether right.
The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the LORD hath made even both of them.
Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty; open thy eyes, thou shalt be satisfied with bread.
nothing, nothing, saith the buyer: but when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.
There is gold, and an abundance of rubies: but the lips of knowledge a precious jewel.
Take his garment that is surety a stranger: and take a pledge of him for an adulteress.

Bread of deceit sweet to a man; but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.
deceit: Heb. lying, or, falsehood
purpose is established by counsel: and with good advice make war.

He that goeth about a talebearer revealeth secrets: therefore meddle not with him that flattereth with his lips.
flattereth: or, enticeth

Whoever curseth his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in obscure darkness.
lamp: or, candle
An inheritance gotten hastily at the beginning; but the end of it shall not be blessed.
Say not thou, I will recompense evil; wait on the LORD, and he shall save thee.

Differing weights an abomination to the LORD; and a false balance not good.
a false…: Heb. balance of deceit
Man’s goings of the LORD; how can a man then understand his own way?
a snare to the man devoureth holy, and after vows to make enquiry.
A wise king scattereth the wicked, and bringeth the wheel over them.

The spirit of man the lamp of the LORD, searching all the inward parts of the belly.
candle: or, lamp
Mercy and truth preserve the king: and his throne is upheld by mercy.
The glory of young men their strength: and the beauty of old men the gray head.

The blueness of a wound cleanseth away evil: so stripes the inward parts of the belly.
cleanseth…: Heb. is a purging medicine against
